clue.text: Girl with a name in new fresco, nothing less

indicators.note: the article and name abbreviation are placed inside the rearranged letters
something made new is remade, so the letters of fresco are rearranged
less means without, so the round letter for nothing is dropped from fresco

parts.note: taken as written before the zero is removed
nothing is zero, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A girl's name is being painted into a fresh mural, at no extra cost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nothing less' drops the zero, 'new' shuffles what remains, and 'in' sets the article and name inside; the surface's painted fresco is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Frances is a common female given name, so a girl may bear it.

parts.note: the most banknotes one hand can grab, also the title of a famous Sergio Leone spaghetti western of 1964

explanation.surface: A gunslinger grabs as many greenbacks as one hand can hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The film A Fistful of Dollars, starring Clint Eastwood, is a classic western; literally the phrase is as much as a clenched hand can hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A clenched hand full of notes is the most one grip can carry, and the Leone film title supplies the western.

clue.text: American intern treated this old hearty

indicators.note: treated as in processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US hospital trainee has been looking after an elderly sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' looks like medical care for the intern's patient but is the anagram signal; 'hearty' is an old word for a sailor, as in 'me hearties'.
explanation.definitionFit: Coleridge's Rime tells of an aged seaman, and a hearty is a jolly sailor, so the old hearty is that poem's mariner.

indicators.note: damaged means knocked out of shape, so the four letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A roadside marker that was once damaged by a passing car.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic cones are placed on roads to mark lanes and roadworks.

indicators.note: torn up means ripped apart, so the letters of the word are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Posted notices have been ripped down in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage of a book or piece of music is a part or extract of it.

explanation.surface: Someone is inclined to be dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural inclination or talent is a bent, and something bent is not straight, also slang for dishonest.

explanation.surface: Asking what stance a family member takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing is posture or manner, and also relevance or connection, as in 'has no bearing on the case'.

indicators.note: cooking means fiddling or doctoring, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its apostrophe dropped supplies all four letters

explanation.surface: Someone notices the aroma of their own cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like the source of the smell, but it means 'cooking the books', the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is called its nose, and to nose is to sniff something out.

clue.text: Cuts in energy twice bring blackout

indicators.note: in places the trimming word inside the doubled energy letter
twice means the energy symbol appears two times

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
cuts means clips, as with shears

explanation.surface: Repeated reductions in power supply lead to a blackout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives EE, and 'in' puts CLIPS between the two Es.
explanation.definitionFit: During a solar eclipse the sun's light is blotted out, a kind of darkness.

clue.text: Agency of Foreign Office supporting alliance

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: a marriage is an alliance between two people or families
bureau is the French word for office, hence foreign

explanation.surface: A government department abroad is backing an international pact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign Office' wants to be the UK ministry; it is a foreign word for office.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaking firm introducing people seeking partners is a business service of that kind.

clue.text: Carelessly, can miss so called deliveries

indicators.note: carelessly means done in a slapdash way, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: A postman's sloppy work means so-called deliveries can go astray.
explanation.definitionFit: Slower, cheaper post is sent by the lower tier of the Royal Mail service, letters delivered to the door.

clue.text: Mid-off takes field in unpleasant jumper

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word off is taken

parts.note: a lea is a poetic word for a meadow or field

explanation.surface: A cricket fielder at mid-off is wearing a nasty sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: Mid-off is a cricket fielding position, but here 'Mid-' just picks the middle of 'off'; 'jumper' looks like a British sweater but is an insect that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting parasite that leaps between hosts is an insect few welcome.

clue.text: Edge of motorway illuminated all round

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so lit encloses the motorway letters

parts.note: illuminated means lit up
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: The hard shoulder of a motorway is lit up along its length.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a motorway from London to Leeds; the 1 is read as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary or outermost extent is the furthest point allowed.

clue.text: Wife to strike for a shoulder-stole?

parts.note: to rap is to knock or strike

explanation.surface: A husband threatens his spouse over the theft of a scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoulder-stole' reads like a theft but a stole is a scarf worn on the shoulders.
explanation.definitionFit: A shawl or scarf draped round the shoulders is an outer covering of that kind.

explanation.surface: A musician's private room, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is whimsical: a cellist plays with a bow, so is one who bows.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a lady's private chamber or a leafy arbour, and a string player wields a bow.

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

explanation.surface: An ancient tree stands on the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest version of something is the initial one.

explanation.surface: A tailor is asked to drop a hem.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower a rope is to pay it out downward, and dressmakers release a hem to make a garment longer.

parts.note: stern means grim or forbidding
an ace is an expert or champion

explanation.surface: A severe winner pulls a sour expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A twisted facial expression of pain or disgust is a contorted look.

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram material

explanation.surface: We gently loosened a knotted mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tangle' looks like a verb or a knot; it is a type of brown kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangle is a name for kelp, a large marine alga.

clue.text: How to address Italian chap in foreign regions

indicators.note: foreign means strange or alien, so the letters take an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tips on the polite way to greet a man from Italy when abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian equivalent of 'Mr' or 'sir' is the courteous title for a gentleman in Italy.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: knocked means criticised or abused, which is reviled

explanation.surface: Someone woke a neighbour by banging on the door to raise the alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked up' looks like one phrase (woken by knocking); 'up' turns REVILED round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To save or set free is to rescue, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

parts.note: a person's estate is their assets or property

explanation.surface: Dogs are kept on a country estate in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Basset hounds are short-legged scent dogs, each a breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Tablets dished out in Bosworth and Hastings, possibly

indicators.note: dished out means distributed, so the letters are spread out anew

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pills were handed out at two historic English sites.
explanation.walkthrough: Bosworth (1485) and Hastings (1066) are famous English battlefields; 'possibly' marks them as examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are famous armed clashes of English history, examples of the plural answer.

clue.text: Presents arms with an instrument on board

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the following letters go inside the steamship letters

parts.note: a ship is boarded, and SS stands for steamship
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A soldier on a ship stands to attention with a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the convention for putting letters inside SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier who presents arms honours someone with a formal military greeting.

clue.text: Bottle of Greek and Italian vermouth

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A bottle of vermouth from Greece and Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like a container; it is British slang for courage. 'Gin and It' is gin with Italian vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle in British slang is nerve or courage, the same as determination.

clue.text: Loud stringed instrument that is played in the wind

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a lute is a plucked stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A noisy guitar-like instrument is strummed outdoors in a breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' suggests outdoors; it means in the woodwind section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind players blow across this instrument, so it belongs to the wind section.

indicators.note: in says the letters are found within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone is stuffed after an awful lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Having eaten enough means being satisfied and no longer hungry.

indicators.note: of signals a run taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: Asking whether men with beards usually have the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans the end of 'bearded' and the start of 'generally', across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an edge over rivals means holding the advantage.

explanation.surface: Renown motivates someone each springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: A spur makes a horse spring forward; Milton's Lycidas says 'Fame is the spur that the clear spirit doth raise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider's goad prompts a horse to leap, and Milton called renown the goad of the noble mind.

clue.text: Accomplished event, going too far in darkroom

parts.note: something accomplished is finished, over
a development is a new event or happening

explanation.surface: A photographer achieved something by leaving prints too long in the darkroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In photography, leaving film too long in developer makes it too dense.
explanation.definitionFit: Excess processing of film in the darkroom makes negatives too dark, an excess of chemical treatment.

explanation.surface: A river wears its banks away.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham and Sunderland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear flows through County Durham, and wear is gradual damage from use or friction.

explanation.surface: Young growths that will become vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'greens' points to Brussels sprouts, the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: New growths on plants are young shoots, and Brussels sprouts are green vegetables.
